EXPLANATION:  
The spectrum shows:  
• Very strong bands at 695 cm⁻¹ and 662 cm⁻¹ – typical region/intensity for aromatic C-Cl stretching vibrations; two distinct bands are expected when more than one C–Cl bond is present.  
• A strong band at 911 cm⁻¹ – characteristic C–H out-of-plane bend for 1,3,5-trisubstituted (2,4,6-substituted) phenyl rings, consistent with a 2,4,6-substituted phenol.  
• Bands at 1134 cm⁻¹ and 1235 cm⁻¹ – match phenolic C–O stretching / in-plane C–O–H bending found near 1150–1250 cm⁻¹.  
• Band at 1595 cm⁻¹ – aromatic C=C ring stretch.  
• C–H stretching at 3073 cm⁻¹ confirms aromatic C–H bonds.  
Among the candidates, only compound 6 (Oc1c(Cl)cc(Cl)cc1Cl, 2,4,6-trichlorophenol) contains an aromatic OH and three C–Cl bonds giving multiple strong Cl–C stretches, and it possesses the 1,3,5-substitution pattern that accounts for the intense ~910 cm⁻¹ band. Compounds lacking Cl cannot explain the dominant 660–700 cm⁻¹ doublet, while those with fewer chlorines or additional strong C–F/S=O features are less consistent with the observed peak set. Hence candidate 6 best fits the Raman evidence.
